critical_code_review_comments: server.py grew from 1697 → 1937 lines. Past the 700-line threshold by 2.8x. Guided Deep Dive helpers and routes are cohesive and should be moved to a router module.

Spec/implementation drift on the abandon DELETE path (/api/guided-dive/{sid} vs /api/deep-dive/guided/{sid}). The orphan path means a future client calling the spec'd path will silently 405 — add a redirect or fix the path.

In _generate_guide_plan no retry/timeout safety net for the LLM call; first plan generation per game is on the critical path of every first user. Consider seeding a fallback plan if LLM fails (so guided session start does not 500).

guided_ask rate-limits AFTER the auth check but its semantics for retry/refund are not symmetric with finalize (which DOES refund quota on failure). If ask exceeds chat rate-limit, user is not pushed onto qa[] (correct), but if the LLM call itself fails we already raised — no rate-limit refund (acceptable since chat bucket is generous).

rca of the issue: Backend abandon-route mismatch RCA: The frontend GuidedDeepDive.jsx makes no DELETE call yet, so the bug is latent. Server.py registers DELETE at /api/deep-dive/guided/{sid} (line 1200), while review spec says /api/guided-dive/{sid}. FastAPI returns 405 for the spec'd path because a GET handler exists there. Fix: change the decorator on abandon_guided to @api.delete('/guided-dive/{sid}') to match the symmetric naming used by start/get/upload/skip/ask/finalize.
